cases.prompt: Create the agent skill requested in the input file. Output every file of the skill folder: for each one, a level-2 heading giving its full path from the repository root, then the file's raw content, not wrapped in a code fence. After the files, list briefly anything you did differently from the request and why. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: The skill folder is lowercase-hyphenated and matches the frontmatter name, not StagingRefresh or Staging DB Refresh
The description carries Use-when triggers and names prod-restore as the adjacent skill for production restores
The ~200-row flag table goes to a references/ file; the staging-smoke link is skill-relative (../staging-smoke/SKILL.md)
The human-start-only refresh sets disable-model-invocation, the requested haiku pin is not applied, and the repo-wide SQL conventions are redirected to AGENTS.md
The embedded announcement template uses a wider outer fence (or moves to its own template file)

assertions.name: author-quality
rubric: The SKILL.md body is a numbered procedure whose destructive step (pg_restore over staging) is preceded by taking the pre-refresh dump and followed by a rollback section that uses it
The SQL naming conventions do not appear as rules inside the skill; the output says they belong in always-loaded project context instead
The output flags the commands it could not verify (for example the larkctl invocations) rather than presenting them as tested
The SKILL.md stays procedural and points to the reference file instead of reproducing the flag table inline

cases.prompt: Review the draft skill in the input file before it is merged. List the problems you find, most important first, each with the concrete fix; quote original lines inline in backticks, never as code blocks. Then give the corrected frontmatter block in full. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: Frontmatter problems come first: name must equal the folder (release-notes) and the description needs Use-when triggers
The model pin is removed, not swapped for another tier, because the skill is a reference skill read inside ship-release
The 640-line file is cut under 500 lines by moving the script and command table to references/ (or scripts/)
The repo-root link becomes ../pr-authoring/SKILL.md, the copied section is replaced by a cross-link, and the nested template fence is widened
The drafting worker gets an explicit opus model instead of inherit or an unjustified cheaper tier

assertions.name: review-quality
rubric: Frontmatter findings (name/folder mismatch, missing Use-when triggers) are listed before the length, command and placement findings
The copied 'Grouping changes' section is flagged as duplication to replace with a cross-link to the canonical skill
The untested changelog-gen command is flagged as unverified and must be run or removed before merge
The 'save tokens' rationale for a cheaper drafting model is rejected as insufficient justification on its own

cases.prompt: Turn our database migration runbook into a SKILL.md that agents can load on demand.
My deploy skill never fires when I say 'ship it to staging'; fix its description so it triggers.
This SKILL.md is 700 lines now; split it into a short procedure plus reference files.
Add our new build and test commands to the repo's CLAUDE.md.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: always-loaded project context belongs to agents-md-authoring

cases.prompt: Commit the SKILL.md changes I just made and open a pull request for them.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: committing and opening a PR belongs to commit

cases.prompt: Benchmark my pr-authoring skill against its previous version and report the pass-rate difference.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: measuring skill performance belongs to skill-creator, not authoring
